q: In the Calvin cycle, Rubisco fixes CO2 onto which acceptor?
explain: Rubisco carboxylates RuBP; the product splits into 2 × 3-PGA. [Wikipedia: Calvin cycle]

q: The physiologically ACTIVE form of phytochrome and its absorption maximum:
explain: Pr (λmax 665 nm) is the inactive red-absorbing form; red light converts it to active Pfr (λmax 730 nm), which moves into the nucleus. [Wikipedia: Phytochrome]

asked: triple response 2015 (P2 Q5c), 2024 (P2 Q5a); ethylene 2021 (P2 Q6a)
q: Which is NOT part of ethylene's "triple response" in dark-grown seedlings?

asked: CAM 2024 (P2 Q6c "CAM is an adaptation to desert life"); CO2-concentrating mechanisms 2023 (P2 Q7a)
q:
Consider:
1. In full CAM, stomata open at night and CO2 is stored as malic acid in the vacuole.
2. By day, with stomata shut, malate is decarboxylated and the CO2 enters the Calvin cycle.
3. CAM separates the two carboxylations spatially, between two cell types, exactly as C4 does.
4. Both CAM and C4 concentrate CO2 around Rubisco.
explain: CAM separates the carboxylations in TIME (temporal), not space. C4 is the spatial one. [Wikipedia: Crassulacean acid metabolism]
subject: Botany

asked: 2021 P2 Q7c "C2 cycle returns to the C3 cycle three-quarters of the carbon lost as glycolate"
q:
Which statements about the photorespiratory (C2) cycle are correct?
1. It runs across chloroplast, peroxisome and mitochondrion.
2. In the mitochondrion, two glycines give one serine, releasing CO2 and NH3.
3. Of the 4 carbons in two phosphoglycolates, 3 return to the Calvin cycle as 3-PGA.
4. Glycine decarboxylation takes place in the peroxisome.
explain: Glycine decarboxylase works in the mitochondrion, not the peroxisome. 3 of 4 C are salvaged, which is the "three-quarters" in the PYQ. [Wikipedia: Photorespiration; Calvin cycle]

asked: inversions 2015 (P2 Q2b, 20 m), 2017 (P2 Q2b), 2019 (P2 Q3b)
q:
Consider:
1. A paracentric inversion does not include the centromere.
2. A crossover inside a paracentric inversion loop gives one dicentric and one acentric chromatid.
3. A pericentric inversion includes the centromere.
4. A dicentric bridge at anaphase I is the typical result of a crossover in a pericentric loop.
explain: A crossover in a pericentric loop gives deletions and duplications, not a dicentric bridge. [Wikipedia: Chromosomal inversion]

AACC, from B. juncea × B. oleracea

asked: linkage / three-point test cross 2020 (P2 Q4a, 20 m), 2018 (P2 Q3a), 2023 (P2 Q3a); crossing over 2021, 2014
q: In a three-point test cross of 1,000 progeny, recombination a–b = 0.20 and b–c = 0.10. Ten double crossovers are observed. Interference is:
explain: Expected DCO = 0.20 × 0.10 × 1000 = 20. Coefficient of coincidence = 10/20 = 0.5. Interference = 1 − c.o.c. = 0.5. [Wikipedia: Coefficient of coincidence]

asked: alpha/beta/gamma 2019 (P2 Q5c), 2020 (P2 Q6a, 20 m)
q:
Consider:
1. The terms α, β and γ diversity were introduced by R. H. Whittaker.
2. In Whittaker's simplest definition, β = γ / α.
3. γ diversity is the mean species diversity per local site.
4. β diversity expresses differentiation (turnover) among local sites.
explain: γ is the TOTAL diversity of the landscape. α is the mean per site. [Wikipedia: Beta diversity; Gamma diversity]

q:

asked: prions 2015 (P2 Q1a "why prions are not viruses"), 2019 (P2 Q4a, 20 m), 2024 (P2 Q3c)
q:

2. Infectious PrP resists proteases, while normal PrPC is readily digested by proteinase K.
3. The word "prion" was coined by Stanley Prusiner in 1982.
4. Prions multiply by reverse-transcribing an RNA template.
explain: Prions have no nucleic acid at all (no DNA or RNA). CJD (humans) and BSE (cattle) are prion diseases. [Wikipedia: Prion]

4. LER is the sum of each crop's intercrop/sole yield ratio

asked: Reclamation of saline & sodic soils: IFoS 2023; sodic soils also IFoS 2005, 2012, 2015, 2016, CSE 2018, 2019
q:
Consider, about reclaiming alkali soils:
1. Gypsum supplies Ca2+ that replaces Na+ on the exchange complex.
2. Gypsum converts sodium carbonate to sodium sulphate, a neutral salt.
3. Enough drainage (natural or subsurface) is needed.
4. Pyrite cannot be used because it raises soil pH.
explain: Pyrite is an acidifying mineral that can be used to reclaim alkaline soils; it lowers pH. [Wikipedia: Alkali soil]
